{
  "root_cause": "The modal's focus trap only returns focus to the modal element when focus leaves, which has tabindex=-1 and is skipped during sequential keyboard navigation. Consequently, Shift+Tab from the first focusable element moves focus to the element that opened the modal instead of wrapping to the last focusable element inside the modal.",
  "repair_strategy": "Augment the modal's _enforceFocus method to retain the existing focusin listener (for mouse clicks) and add a namespaced keydown listener that intercepts Tab and Shift+Tab keys. When the user attempts to leave the modal via Tab at the last focusable element or Shift+Tab at the first focusable element, prevent default and move focus to the opposite end of the modal's focusable set, ensuring cyclic navigation within the modal.",
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Shift+Tab from the first focusable control in the confirmation dialog will now move focus to the last focusable control (the Delete button), allowing users to navigate continuously within the modal using only the keyboard, satisfying ARIA modal design practices.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "Potential conflict with custom keyboard handling of Tab inside the modal.",
    "If the modal contains no focusable elements, the keydown listener will early‑exit, leaving behavior unchanged.",
    "Minimal performance overhead from querying focusable elements on each keydown (acceptable for typical modal size).",
    "If the modal is disposed without removing the keydown listener, a stray listener could remain; however, the listener is namespaced with '.modal' and will be cleared by the existing dispose logic that offs events matching the modal's EVENT_KEY."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "Verify that Shift+Tab from the first focusable element (the Close button) moves focus to the last focusable element (the Delete button).",
    "Verify that Tab from the last focusable element (the Delete button) moves focus to the first focusable element (the Close button).",
    "Confirm that clicking outside the modal and then pressing Tab returns focus to the first focusable element inside the modal.",
    "Ensure that the modal's dismissal via Escape, backdrop click, or Cancel/Delete buttons continues to work as expected.",
    "Check that screen readers announce the modal and its contents when it opens.",
    "Validate that the modal can be opened and closed multiple times without losing the wrap behavior."
  ]
}
